Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Request: remove a single conversation from logs (RQ-591)

Hi Nikhil,

We discovered a thread in our integration logs that contains PHI and is governed by our data residency requirements. We'd like Redwood to remove the single conversation referenced in Support Request RQ-591 (internal ID: convo-20270215-ML). Can you confirm what you need from us to action a surgical excision of that conversation from your telemetry/audit logs?

Attached is a CSV export of the conversation metadata and a redacted snippet (conversation_export_RQ591.txt). We can also provide a signed authorization if required.

Key ask: remove the conversation across all telemetry/aggregation layers (token logs, request traces, activity stream) and provide an audit entry showing the excision (or a redaction confirmation).

Thanks,
Alice Brooks
Security & Compliance, MediCore Health
alice.brooks@medicore.com
Attachment: conversation_export_RQ591.txt (text/plain)
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Brooks <alice.brooks@medicore.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 10:02:15 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: remove a single conversation from logs (RQ-591)

Hi Alice — thanks for the detail and the export.

Short answer: we can perform a targeted excision for a single conversation under a data residency/retention exception, but we need a couple of items before we run the procedure: 1) explicit written authorization (signed) from a MediCore security/business owner; 2) the exact conversation/request IDs (you included convo-20270215-ML — can you confirm that is the primary id we should operate against?); and 3) a confirmation of the environments to include (hosted API logs, analytics aggregation, and any customer-specific dedicated telemetry).

Proposed plan (high level):
- Step 0: Intake & authorization check (you provide signed_authorization_MediCore_20270402.pdf)
- Step 1: Freeze ingestion for affected IDs to avoid new writes (short maintenance window)
- Step 2: Run targeted excision job against token logs, request traces, and activity stream
- Step 3: Re-index aggregates and invalidate cache entries (if any)
- Step 4: Produce an audit artifact with hash of removed entries and a job run id for your records

Estimated SLA: 48–72 business hours after we have signed authorization and confirmation of IDs. If you need expedited handling we can request an override; please indicate urgency.

Looping in Monica from Compliance (monica_patel@redwood.ai) to coordinate approvals and the execution window. Laura Bennett from Platform Ops will be on-call for the excision run if we need re-indexing help.

Can you reply with the signed authorization and confirm the target ID? Also let us know whether all environments (hosted + analytics) should be included.

Best,
Nikhil Sharma
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>, Alice Brooks <alice.brooks@medicore.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 14:27:45 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: remove a single conversation from logs (RQ-591)

Thanks Nikhil and Alice — I reviewed the export. Monica here from Compliance — short checklist and execution notes below: 

Checklist for excision (must be present):
- Signed authorization from the customer (legal sign-off accepted) — we can accept the attached PDF you mentioned.
- Exact conversation/request ids to drop (please confirm convo-20270215-ML).
- Confirmation which retention layers to include: token logs (raw), request traces (trace-store), and aggregated analytics (daily indices).

Execution notes:
- We'll run the excision on a staging mirror first and validate that aggregates reconcile. If staging run is clean, we'll schedule the production window (typically 30–60 minutes).
- We will produce a removal job id (RJ-20270402-591) and an audit package: a signed manifest (SHA256 hash) that lists removed object keys. We record the operation in the customer-facing support case SC-591.
- After the excision, we will keep a retention-exception record for 7 days for internal audit (not queryable by customer) and then purge that internal record; this is standard for transparency during compliance ops.

Please confirm: 
- Alice: signed_authorization_MediCore_20270402.pdf is acceptable and confirms convo-20270215-ML; and
- Laura: availability for the production window on Mon 2027-04-05 02:00–04:00 UTC (we may shift earlier if customer requests).

Attachment accepted: signed_authorization_MediCore_20270402.pdf (customer signature present).

If all good, we will set RJ-20270402-591 and target a production excision within 48 hours.

— Monica Patel
Compliance Lead, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai
Attachment: signed_authorization_MediCore_20270402.pdf (application/pdf)

Monica/Nikhil — confirmed and thanks for the clear plan.

I confirm: signed_authorization_MediCore_20270402.pdf is attached and authorizes Redwood to excise convo-20270215-ML across hosted logs, request traces, and analytics indices. We also request an expedited window if RJ-20270402-591 can be run before EOD Monday local to Redwood. Please confirm once the job completes and share the audit manifest.

Thanks again — this is time-sensitive for our incident review.
